glanceLede: Single-family homes and condos/townhomes are sending different signals. Here are the four key measures for each, side by side.

verdicts.label: Single-family homes
verdicts.note: Supply down from {{ s.sfh.m.monthsSupply.prior | dec1 }} months; sales closed at {{ s.sfh.m.olpReceived.current | dec1 }}% of original list price; contract time fell from {{ s.sfh.m.daysToContract.prior }} to {{ s.sfh.m.daysToContract.current }} days.

verdicts.label: Condos & townhomes
verdicts.note: Supply down from {{ s.condo.m.monthsSupply.prior | dec1 }} months but still elevated; contract time rose from {{ s.condo.m.daysToContract.prior }} to {{ s.condo.m.daysToContract.current }} days.

numbersLede: Every figure below is as reported for St. Lucie County. Percent change is year over year, {{ dataMonth }} versus {{ priorMonth }}.

insights.heading: What the Market Is Telling Us
insights.lede: What the {{ dataMonth }} figures point to, tied directly to the tables on page 3.

cards.title: Single-family: near balanced, tilting toward sellers.
cards.body: Supply eased from {{ s.sfh.m.monthsSupply.prior | dec1 }} to {{ s.sfh.m.monthsSupply.current | dec1 }} months. The typical sale closed at {{ s.sfh.m.olpReceived.current | dec1 }}% of original list price, up from {{ s.sfh.m.olpReceived.prior | dec1 }}%, and median days to contract fell {{ s.sfh.m.daysToContract.pct | abspct }} to {{ s.sfh.m.daysToContract.current }}. Both support the seller tilt.

cards.title: Single-family prices held essentially steady.
cards.body: The median sale price was {{ s.sfh.m.medianPrice.current | usd }}, compared with {{ s.sfh.m.medianPrice.prior | usd }} a year earlier, while closed sales slipped {{ s.sfh.m.closedSales.pct | abspct }} to {{ s.sfh.m.closedSales.current | int }}.

cards.title: Condos and townhomes remain buyer-leaning.
cards.body: Active inventory fell {{ s.condo.m.inventory.pct | abspct }} to {{ s.condo.m.inventory.current | int }} and supply dropped from {{ s.condo.m.monthsSupply.prior | dec1 }} months, yet {{ s.condo.m.monthsSupply.current | dec1 }} months still leaves buyers with options. Median days to contract lengthened to {{ s.condo.m.daysToContract.current }} from {{ s.condo.m.daysToContract.prior }}, which makes precise pricing essential.

cards.title: Read the {{ s.condo.m.medianPrice.pct | signed }} condo median in context.
cards.body: The median rose to {{ s.condo.m.medianPrice.current | usd }} from {{ s.condo.m.medianPrice.prior | usd }}, but it is based on {{ s.condo.m.closedSales.current | int }} closings. Read it alongside {{ s.condo.m.monthsSupply.current | dec1 }} months of supply, {{ s.condo.m.inventory.current | int }} active listings and {{ s.condo.m.olpReceived.current | dec1 }}% of original list price, not as a universal increase in condo values.

cards.title: Cash plays a very different role by property type.
cards.body: {{ cash.sfh }}% of single-family closings ({{ s.sfh.m.paidInCash.current | int }} of {{ s.sfh.m.closedSales.current | int }}) and {{ cash.condo }}% of condo/townhome closings ({{ s.condo.m.paidInCash.current | int }} of {{ s.condo.m.closedSales.current | int }}) were paid in cash, calculated from the reported counts.

insights.localLine: County figures blend varied local markets, such as Port St. Lucie, Fort Pierce, Tradition and Hutchinson Island, and conditions in any one of them can differ from the county median.

guidanceLede: The same county data calls for different moves depending on which side of the transaction you are on, and which property type you are dealing with.

sfh: At {{ s.sfh.m.monthsSupply.current | dec1 }} months of supply and {{ s.sfh.m.daysToContract.current }} median days to contract, well-priced homes move. Have a pre-approval or proof of funds ready.
Sales closed at {{ s.sfh.m.olpReceived.current | dec1 }}% of original list price, so there may be less room than you expect. {{ cash.sfh }}% of closings were cash (calculated).
condo: At {{ s.condo.m.monthsSupply.current | dec1 }} months of supply and {{ s.condo.m.daysToContract.current }} median days to contract, buyers can often negotiate on price, credits or repairs.
The {{ s.condo.m.medianPrice.pct | signed }} median reflects {{ s.condo.m.closedSales.current | int }} closings. Judge each unit on its building's recent sales, budget, reserves and assessments.

sfh: The market tilts your way, narrowly.
At {{ s.sfh.m.monthsSupply.current | dec1 }} months of supply, near balanced, homes priced to recent closed sales are closing at {{ s.sfh.m.olpReceived.current | dec1 }}% of original list price.
Median days to contract fell to {{ s.sfh.m.daysToContract.current }}. A realistic first price helps you capture early buyer attention.
condo: With {{ s.condo.m.monthsSupply.current | dec1 }} months of supply and {{ s.condo.m.daysToContract.current }} median days to contract, buyers have options. Precise pricing matters more than usual.

The {{ s.condo.m.medianPrice.pct | signed }} median rests on {{ s.condo.m.closedSales.current | int }} closings. Price from comparable sales in your building or community, with association documents ready.
